# AV Gen tool catalogue

<!-- Generated by `avgen --describe all --out .` (tools/gen_api.sh). Do not edit by hand: tests/unit/test_api_catalogue.cpp fails when this file and the engine disagree. -->

API level 2, engine 0.3.0. Machine-readable form: `schemas/tool-catalogue.json`; the error codes are in [errors.md](errors.md).

Every call through a session returns the same envelope (ADR-2153): `{success, result, summary, changes, warnings, transaction, job}`, and on failure `error: {code, message, recovery, details?}` with `result` null. Arguments are validated against the input schema before the tool runs. **Requirements** are what the host must provide for a tool to be available (a composition, or a host hook); `session.info` answers supported, available and permitted per tool.

**Execution class** says how a call is scheduled: `read` (no change), `instant` (a value, applied at the next frame), `rebind` (a route, key or shot added or removed), `structural` (the composition is rebuilt), `session` (changes the session, not the project: open, save, import, seek) and `job` (seconds to minutes: a child process or a render). **Permissions** are what a session must allow: `read` and `write` (files the caller names), `subprocess`, `gpu`.

### `asset.import`: Import an asset into the project

MCP name `asset_import`. Class `session`. Permissions: `read`, `write`. Requires: nothing. Since API 2. Flags: mutatesSession, idempotent.

Copy a supported model, environment or texture into the open project's assets/<type>/ folder and record it in assets/manifest.json. `file` is any path this session may read (a relative path resolves against the open project's folder). The original is never modified. Returns the asset's id, asset://project/<type>/<file>.<ext>, which every asset-taking tool accepts; importing the same bytes again returns the existing file's id. A model is loaded by the engine before the call succeeds, and `import` reports what it found (meshes, rigs, joints, clips, materials, triangles, bounds, warnings): a file that does not load is refused and nothing is left behind. `source` records where the file came from in the manifest.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string | yes |  | Path to a reachable model, environment or texture |
| `source` | object |  |  |  |

### `asset.import_audio`: Import audio

MCP name `asset_import_audio`. Class `session`. Permissions: `read`, `write`. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesSession, idempotent.

Copy an audio file into the open project and make it the session's track, then analyze it. Copied rather than referenced on purpose: a project that points at a file on somebody's desktop stops working the day that file moves, and the project format stores a relative path and a hash precisely so it does not have to. Reports the duration, rate and channel count read back from the decoder, because an import that silently decoded nothing is the failure worth catching.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `file` | string |  |  | Path to the audio file, as reported by asset.list_importable |

## audio

### `audio.get_analysis`: Audio analysis

MCP name `audio_get_analysis`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

What the analyzer currently hears: loudness, the five frequency bands (auto-gained, and as long-term levels), spectral centroid, a loudness-independent energy, the onset rate, stereo width, the onset and its register, tempo and beat position in musical time (which beat of which bar), plus when each musical event (beat, downbeat, build, break, drop, impact) last fired. This is the state audio-reactive work is built on.

Input: none.

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `audio.import_stem`: Import an analysis stem

MCP name `audio_import_stem`. Class `session`. Permissions: `read`, `write`. Requires: nothing. Since API 2. Flags: mutatesSession, idempotent.

Copy a stem (one part of the song: drums, bass, ...) into the open project's assets/audio/stems/, record it in assets/manifest.json, and analyse it beside the mix. A stem is analysis only -- never played or mixed -- and publishes its own signals, stem.<key>.* (active, rms, peak, level, onset, onsetStrength, the five bands, centroid, width, onsetLow/Mid/High), which `signals` lists as they are on the bus now; route them with modulation.create. `key` is that identity: lower-case letters, digits and _, unique in the project, and never changed by a relabel. `role` (default other) is the artist's statement of what the stem is, never inferred; role.<role>.* follows the first stem of each role. Importing the same bytes again reuses the project's copy. The stem is session state: project.save keeps it (assets.stems), and a rollback does not remove it.

### `audio.remove_stem`: Remove an analysis stem

MCP name `audio_remove_stem`. Class `session`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 2. Flags: mutatesSession, destructive.

Take a stem out of the project's analysis list. Its file stays in the project's assets (another stem or a later import may use it). The bus cannot undeclare a name, so its stem.<key>.* signals stay listed and read 0 (inactive) from now on: a route on one does nothing, and `routes` counts them. Session state, like the import: project.save writes the list without it.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `key` | string | yes |  | The stem's key, from audio.list_stems |

Output schema: `{"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"key":{"description":"The stem removed","type":"string"},"remaining":{"description":"Stems left in the project","type":"integer"},"routes":{"description":"Modulation routes whose source is one of its stem.<key>.* signals; each now reads 0","type":"integer"}},"required":["key","remaining","routes"],"type":"object"}`

### `camera.get`: Camera state

MCP name `camera_get`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

The camera's pose, mode, field of view, and the lens, exposure and focus settings that are exposed as parameters. Read this before moving the camera: in orbit mode the position and target parameters are ignored, and the mode is part of the answer.

### `camera.set`: Move the camera

MCP name `camera_set`. Class `instant`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesProject, idempotent, undoable.

Place the camera. Position and target are world-space metres; fovDegrees is the vertical field of view. The camera must be in free mode for an explicit pose to have any effect, so this switches it there and tells you it did. Pass mode explicitly to override.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fovDegrees` | number |  | >= 5.0, <= 120.0 | Vertical field of view |
| `mode` | string, one of `orbit`, `free`, `spline` |  |  | Camera mode |
| `position` | array of number |  |  | Eye position |
| `target` | array of number |  |  | Look-at point |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `camera.frame_node`: Frame a node

MCP name `camera_frame_node`. Class `instant`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesProject, idempotent, undoable.

Point the camera at a node and stand far enough back to fit it in shot. Computes the distance from the node's own world bounds and the current field of view, so it is a framing decision rather than a guessed coordinate. 'margin' widens the shot: 1.0 fits exactly, 1.5 leaves room around the subject.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `azimuthDegrees` | number |  | >= -360.0, <= 360.0 | Compass angle around the subject |
| `elevationDegrees` | number |  | >= -80.0, <= 80.0 | How far above the subject to place the camera |
| `margin` | number |  | >= 1.0, <= 8.0 | Headroom factor (default 1.4) |
| `name` | string | yes |  | Node name from scene.find_nodes |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

## director

### `director.inspect_scene`: Inspect the scene for directing

MCP name `director_inspect_scene`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

What a plan can name and when things happen: every subject (characters, heroes, nodes, cameras, effects) by kind and id, the song's sections as they come round ("chorus 2" is the second time the chorus comes back) with what each one sounds like -- its own energy, and the audio measured under it: a level-free energy, onsets per second (kick, snare, hat), brightness in Hz and each band's level in dB -- the meter (which beat is bar 1, bars per phrase), the piece's length, and the plans this project already holds (revise one by reusing its id). Prefer this over parameter-level inspection when directing.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `kinds` | array of string |  |  | Only these subject kinds; omit for all |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `director.propose_reactivity`: The default audio-reactivity plan

MCP name `director_propose_reactivity`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

The Director's default audio-reactivity plan for this scene (ADR-927), from the reactive catalogue (director.inspect_capabilities, "reactive"): routes at three levels -- hats and claps on small things, the kick and the bar on the heroes (each hero its own layer, timing and amplitude), the section on the world's light, fog, wind and colour -- with staggered delays and depth that follows the section. Returns the plan (its "routes" and "sources"), the music's layers, a summary and what was left alone and why. Changes nothing: edit the plan if the request asks for something else, then director.propose_plan it for the person's approval.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string |  |  | The plan's id; default "reactivity". Reuse an existing id to revise it |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `director.record_plan`: Record a plan's live performances

MCP name `director_record_plan`. Class `job`. Permissions: none. Requires: `recording`. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, requiresApproval.

Bake a plan whose performances are live (mode goal): play the project from zero on a scratch copy, keep what each character actually did and when its events happened, check the recording plays back and scrubs exactly, and put the RECORDED plan in front of the person for approval. Nothing is applied until they approve. Takes seconds; use it when the person wants a live performance fixed, or wants cues on its events (which only a recording can time).

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `plan` | object | yes |  | A Director Plan (schemaVersion 1); see director.plan_schema |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `director.watch_events`: Watch the film for what happens in it

MCP name `director_watch_events`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: `watch`. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

Play the project from zero on a scratch copy (audio off, nothing changed) and list every world event it raises -- a scenario's beat, a character's named completion, a goal's arrival -- with its time and who raised it. Then propose a plan whose times are {"event": name, "subject": who, "occurrence": n}: the observation is attached to it for you. Takes seconds.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `untilSeconds` | number |  |  | how far to watch; default: the whole piece, at most 240 s |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `director.evaluate`: Evaluate a plan with the quality evaluator

MCP name `director_evaluate`. Class `job`. Permissions: `subprocess`. Requires: `evaluation`. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesSession, expensive.

Render a span of the film with a plan in it -- a candidate you have not proposed ("plan"), or a revision the project already holds ("planId") -- on a scratch copy, and ask the Creative Critic about it. Nothing in the project changes and nothing is proposed: evaluate several candidates, director.compare them, and director.propose_plan only the one that won. Returns the evaluator's headline, dimension scores and findings, each finding keyed by the plan items its time span overlaps; the report is kept with the plan's evaluations. Minutes, not seconds: render the span that matters (a set piece, a section), not the film.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `from` | number | yes |  | film seconds the span starts at |
| `label` | string |  |  | What to call this iteration in comparisons, e.g. "lower hover" |
| `mode` | string |  |  | fast \| preview (default) \| deep: the evaluator's depth |
| `plan` | object |  |  | A Director Plan (schemaVersion 1); see director.plan_schema |
| `planId` | string |  |  | A plan the project holds, evaluated as it is (instead of "plan") |

MCP name `director_propose_plan`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, requiresApproval, deterministic.

Compile a plan against the scene WITHOUT changing it, and put the result in front of the person: what will be added or replaced, and every finding. Nothing is applied until they approve; the task then ends waiting for them. Whatever cannot be built is left out and said, never substituted -- if you want a substitute (a jump for a backflip), propose it as a change and say so. Reuse an existing plan's id to revise it.

## document

### `document.get`: Get a document

MCP name `document_get`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 2. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

The scene or project document as the engine would write it now, with a content hash to compare later reads with. `scene` is Composition::toJson: every key the scene reads, plus the keys it keeps without reading (`_` notes, unknown top-level keys); the shape is schemas/avgen-scene.schema.json, and it is what document.patch paths point into. `project` is the document a project save would write, built without writing anything. Read it before patching.

### `document.validate`: Validate a document

MCP name `document_validate`. Class `job`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 2. Flags: readOnly, idempotent, expensive.

Check a scene or project document without installing it. First against the generated schema (schemas/avgen-<document>.schema.json, with the engine's own validator), then by building it on a private offline engine with its own asset registry: a scene is parsed into a composition and its node assets are resolved as the session's scene resolves them; a project is loaded from a scratch copy whose relative paths are resolved against the open project's folder. Returns structured findings {severity, code, pointer, message, document}; valid is true when none is an error. Unknown scene keys are warnings here (a file on disk is only warned about); document.patch refuses a patch that adds one.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | object | yes |  |  |

### `document.patch`: Patch the scene document

MCP name `document_patch`. Class `structural`. Permissions: none. Requires: `composition`. Since API 2. Flags: mutatesProject, undoable.

Edit the scene by applying an RFC 6902 JSON Patch to its document (document.get {document: scene}), then rebuilding the composition from the result. One contract for every structural edit: add a light (`{op: add, path: /lights/-, value: {...}}`), a node (`/nodes/-`), change a node's tint (`/nodes/<i>/tint`), remove anything. Refused with INVALID_ARGUMENTS and details.pointer when an operation does not apply, when the result has a schema error it did not have before, or when it adds a key the engine does not read; nothing is changed then. Keys the patch does not touch are kept, including `_` notes and unknown top-level keys. The session's parameter overrides survive the rebuild: each is re-applied unless the patch set the value the document carries (overrides.yielded lists those). Routes are kept. dryRun checks the patch, builds the result on a private engine and changes nothing. It runs in the call's transaction, so transaction.rollback restores the pre-patch document. A rebuild restarts entity simulations; a live host refuses it while a show runs.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `document` | string, one of `scene` | yes |  | Only the scene can be patched |
| `dryRun` | boolean |  |  | Check and predict, change nothing |
| `patch` | array of object | yes |  | RFC 6902 operations, applied in order |

## field

### `field.list`: List music influence fields

MCP name `field_list`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: `composition`. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

The fields in the scene and what each resolved to: where it is, how far it reaches, which entities it governs, and -- the part worth reading -- whether it follows something baked or something live. ### `field.create`: Create a music influence field

MCP name `field_create`. Class `structural`. Permissions: none. Requires: `composition`. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesProject, idempotent, undoable.

Put a music influence field in the scene. It scales the depth of the reactions its governed entities already have, so the same `audio.bass -> emissiveGain` an author wrote becomes spatial: full strength at the centre, nothing at the edge, smooth between. Give it a `source` to make it follow a node or entity -- a character carrying the music with them -- and `tags` to say which entities it governs.

| `source` | string |  |  | Node or entity whose position it follows; omit to pin it at `center` |
| `strength` | number |  |  | Gain at full influence (default 1) |
| `tags` | array of string |  |  | Entity tags or profile names it governs; empty means all |

### `modulation.create`: Create a modulation route

MCP name `modulation_create`. Class `rebind`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesProject, idempotent, undoable.

Connect a signal to a parameter so it moves with the music. 'amount' is the depth and may be negative to invert. 'op' says how it meets the parameter's value: add is the usual choice, multiply scales it, replace overwrites it. Use attackMs/decayMs to smooth a jumpy source, and an envelope to turn a momentary event such as music.drop into something that decays rather than flashing for one frame. The route is bound immediately and the result says whether it resolved.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number |  | >= -8.0, <= 8.0 | Depth; negative inverts |
| `attackMs` | number |  | >= 0.0, <= 60000.0 | Rise smoothing, milliseconds |
| `component` | integer |  | >= 0.0, <= 3.0 | Drive only this component (0-based) |
| `decayMs` | number |  | >= 0.0, <= 60000.0 | Fall smoothing, milliseconds |
| `envelope` | string, one of `none`, `peakhold`, `linearfall` |  |  | Turn an event into a falling envelope |
| `envelopeFallPerSecond` | number |  | >= 0.0, <= 100.0 | How fast the envelope falls |
| `op` | string, one of `add`, `multiply`, `replace`, `min`, `max` |  |  | How it combines |
| `polarity` | string, one of `unipolar`, `bipolar` |  |  | Bipolar maps 0..1 to -1..1 first |
| `source` | string | yes |  | Signal name from signal.list, e.g. 'audio.bass' |
| `target` | string | yes |  | Parameter path from parameter.search |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `performance.profile_scene`: Profile the scene for live performance

MCP name `performance_profile_scene`. Class `job`. Permissions: `subprocess`. Requires: `profile`. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, expensive.

Run the live scene profiler (avgen --live-profile) on a scratch copy of the project, in a child process, and return its record (schema avgen.liveprofile/1): frame statistics against the target's budget, the critical path (GPU, CPU or sync), GPU time by category, CPU time by stage, resources, and optimization candidates with ESTIMATED savings (and MEASURED ones when verifyCandidates > 0). Headless by default (deterministic, no present); "live" opens windows and measures the real loop. Seconds to minutes. The editor keeps rendering meanwhile, so the GPU is shared and the numbers are contended: for numbers to quote, run the command with the editor closed.

| `mode` | string, one of `headless`, `live` |  |  | headless (default) or live |
| `quality` | string |  |  | auto, a level (ultra..emergency) or a profile (quality, balanced, performance); default auto |
| `start` | number |  | >= 0.0 | seconds into the piece to measure from (default 0) |
| `targetFps` | number |  | >= 24.0, <= 240.0 | the live target, 24..240 (default 60) |

### `performance.optimize_scene`: Optimize the scene for a frame rate

MCP name `performance_optimize_scene`. Class `job`. Permissions: `subprocess`. Requires: `profile`. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesSession, expensive.

Search lever combinations (avgen --live-profile --optimize, headless, on a scratch copy) for the least MEASURED visual change that reaches the target (budget x 0.9). Every single lever is measured for time (A/B) and picture (ORIGINAL vs OPTIMIZED: pixel, SSIM, edge, luminance incl. matched, temporal, inside the hero boxes); combinations are ESTIMATED from the singles and then MEASURED. Heroes are never degraded by default. With apply=true the chosen levers are added to the project's live ceilings when the answer arrives (never the scene; performance.set_live_quality clearOverrides undoes it). Minutes. The editor shares the GPU meanwhile.

### `project.diff_saved`: Compare with the saved project

MCP name `project_diff_saved`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, expensive.

Serialise the project and compare it with what was last saved or opened: the exact answer to "would a save write anything different?". Expensive (a full serialisation: up to hundreds of milliseconds on a large project), so ask only when it matters -- before closing. session.info's `revisions.dirty` is the cheap answer, and errs only towards dirty: a value edited and then set back. ## render

### `render.probe`: Look at the frame

MCP name `render_probe`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: `composition`. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

What the camera can currently see, as numbers: which nodes fall inside the frustum, where each sits in the frame, and how much of the height it fills. Use it to check a shot frames its subject before trusting that it does -- a camera pointed at nothing reports nothing rather than looking fine. Without `time` or `frame` it reads the camera the last frame used, the same as camera.get, so after moving the camera let a frame happen before asking what it sees. With `time` (or `frame` at `fps`) it evaluates the session's project as it is now -- unsaved edits included -- on a fresh offline engine at that time, exactly as a render's frame there is evaluated (history seek), so the rectangle is the one render.capture will draw: use it on a host that runs no frames (avgen serve). With `width` and `height` each rectangle is also given in pixels.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `aspect` | number |  |  | Frame aspect ratio (default 16:9, or width/height) |
| `fps` | number |  | >= 0.001 | The rate `frame` counts in (default: the project's render fps) |
| `frame` | integer |  | >= 0.0 | Evaluate at this frame (at `fps`) on a fresh engine |
| `height` | integer |  | >= 1.0, <= 16384.0 | The frame's height in pixels: adds a pixel rectangle |
| `limit` | integer |  | >= 1.0, <= 200.0 | Maximum nodes reported (default 40) |
| `node` | string |  |  | Ask about one node; omit for everything visible |
| `time` | number |  | >= 0.0 | Evaluate the scene at this time (seconds) on a fresh engine |
| `width` | integer |  | >= 1.0, <= 16384.0 | The frame's width in pixels: adds a pixel rectangle |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `render.capture`: Capture a frame

MCP name `render_capture`. Class `job`. Permissions: `gpu`, `write`. Requires: `composition`. Since API 2. Flags: mutatesSession, expensive, supportsCancellation, supportsProgress, deterministic.

Render one frame of the project as it is in this session -- unsaved edits included; nothing is saved -- to a PNG (or EXR, by the path's extension), through the same offline render path a sequence uses, so the frame hash equals that frame's hash in a render.start sequence. Give `frame` (at `fps`) or `time` (seconds); neither is time 0. `history: play` (the default) first renders and discards every frame from 0, so the frame has the history a play-through had (cost grows with the time); `seek` jumps there, which is fast but may differ slightly on stateful content (envelopes, simulations). Returns a job id at once: job.wait for the result (frame hash, file sha256, timing). The size, rate and tier default to the project's render settings.

| `height` | integer |  | >= 1.0, <= 16384.0 | Pixels (default: the project's render height) |
| `history` | string, one of `play`, `seek` |  |  | play (default): render from 0 and keep the last frame; seek: jump to the frame |
| `path` | string | yes |  | The image to write, .png or .exr; relative to the project folder; inside a write root |
| `tier` | string, one of `preview`, `realtime`, `high`, `offline` |  |  | Quality tier (default: the project's, normally offline) |
| `time` | number |  | >= 0.0 | Seconds; used when `frame` is not given |
| `width` | integer |  | >= 1.0, <= 16384.0 | Pixels (default: the project's render width) |

### `render.start`: Render a sequence

MCP name `render_start`. Class `job`. Permissions: `gpu`, `write`. Requires: `composition`. Since API 2. Flags: mutatesSession, expensive, supportsCancellation, supportsProgress, deterministic.

Render a range of the project as it is in this session (unsaved edits included; nothing is saved) to a PNG or EXR sequence in a folder (frame_000000.png, numbered from the range's first frame) or to a video file. `range` is "start:end" in seconds, end exclusive, as --range is. ## scene

### `scene.create_node`: Create a node

MCP name `scene_create_node`. Class `structural`. Permissions: `read`. Requires: `composition`. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesProject, idempotent, undoable.

Put an object in the scene: a glTF asset, or an empty Group to parent things to. `asset` is an asset://project/ id (what asset.import returns) or a path; a relative path resolves against the open project's folder, never the working directory. It is resolved against the folders this session may read, so a model that is not reachable is refused here rather than becoming a node that renders nothing. Reports the node's world bounds, read back from the built node.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `asset` | string |  |  | asset://project/ id or path of the .gltf/.glb, for kind gltf |
| `kind` | string |  |  | gltf (default) or group |
| `name` | string |  |  | Node name; must not already exist |
| `parent` | string |  |  | Parent node name; omit for the root |
| `position` | array of number |  |  | World position |

### `transaction.begin`: Begin a transaction

MCP name `transaction_begin`. Class `session`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesSession.

## transport

### `transport.get_policy`: Time policy

MCP name `transport_get_policy`. Class `read`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

What the world clock does while nothing is playing, and which policies this host offers. running: the transport plays. stopped-ambient: parked, the world keeps moving on the wall clock (rigs, wind, water). stopped-frozen: parked, time does not advance, so two reads with no edit between them agree. stepped: nothing advances until transport.step. offline: the fixed-step clock of a render.

Input: none.

Output schema: `{"additionalProperties":false,"properties":{"effective":{"description":"What governs time now: running while a live transport plays","enum":["running","stopped-frozen","stopped-ambient","stepped","offline"],"type":"string"},"offered":{"description":"What transport.set_policy accepts on this host","items":{"description":"policy","enum":["running","stopped-frozen","stopped-ambient","stepped","offline"],"type":"string"},"type":"array"},"policy":{"description":"The host's setting","enum":["running","stopped-frozen","stopped-ambient","stepped","offline"],"type":"string"},"renderTime":{"description":"The world clock, seconds","type":"number"},"stepped":{"description":"transport.step: frames advanced","type":"integer"}},"required":["policy","effective","offered","renderTime"],"type":"object"}`

MCP name `transport_set_policy`. Class `session`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesSession, idempotent.

Choose what the world clock does while the transport is parked. Refused (FAILED_PRECONDITION) for a policy this host does not offer: transport.get_policy lists them. Never changes a render: every render job has its own offline engine.

### `transport.step`: Step time

MCP name `transport_step`. Class `session`. Permissions: none. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesSession.

Under the stepped policy: advance the world by `frames` frames (or by `seconds`, rounded to whole frames) at `fps` (default: the project's render rate), by PLAYING -- the same update a running frame takes, deltaTime 1/fps each -- not by seeking. renderTime moves by exactly frames/fps. To get the state a playback reaches at time t, step there; sequencer.set_playhead seeks instead.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fps` | number |  | >= 1.0, <= 1000.0 | Frames per second; default the project's render rate |
| `frames` | integer |  | >= 1.0, <= 100000.0 | Frames to advance |
| `seconds` | number |  | >= 0.0 | Or seconds to advance, rounded to whole frames |

## world

### `world.list_recipes`: List world recipes

MCP name `world_list_recipes`. Class `read`. Permissions: `read`. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: readOnly, idempotent.

The world recipes this session can reach, by name. A recipe is a seed, an extent, an asset library and a set of ecology weights; generating one fills a world with what the library allows. Read this before generating rather than guessing a name.

Input: none.

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).

### `world.generate`: Generate a world

MCP name `world_generate`. Class `structural`. Permissions: `read`. Requires: nothing. Since API 1. Flags: mutatesProject, destructive, undoable.

Compose a world from a recipe and install it into the scene, replacing whatever ecology the terrain had. This is the same path as the Generate World button. Reports what was placed, which is the answer worth reading: a recipe whose library has nothing the weights ask for composes successfully and puts nothing in the world.

| Input | Type | Required | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `recipe` | string |  |  | Recipe name, as reported by world.list_recipes |

Output: not yet described (listed in `schemas/tools-without-output-schema.json`).
